biography.plain_text: Miguel Sans Mora was a Spanish industrialist from a Catalan textile family. He chaired Hijos de Francisco Sans and CEPANSA, helping direct a network of cotton-processing businesses across Spain. His daughter María Victoria married into the Quadras family and became Countess of Sant Llorens del Munt, linking two established industrial families.

confidence.reason: Academic industrial history and public family accounts establish roles and family links.

biography.html: Miguel Sans Mora was a Spanish industrialist from a Catalan textile family. long_biography.plain_text:
Miguel Sans Mora's textile interests intersected with his enthusiasm for sailing through a business partnership. A canvas factory belonging to the Sans family joined Eusebi Marsal's Barcelona sailmaking workshop to form La Industrial Velera Marsal in 1945. Sans Mora also brought the maritime historian José María Martínez-Hidalgo into the company, where he became a partner and chairman.

Sans Mora helped organise competitive sailing as well as taking part in it. For more than twenty years, he served as commodore of the Real Club Náutico de Barcelona and president of the Mediterranean's international cruising committee. His racing included the Barcelona-to-Palma competition held after the Spanish Civil War.

confidence.reason: Firsthand family-company interview, maritime museum scholarship and official event history establish distinct business partnership and sustained sporting governance.
